chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Hāshim, from Abū Khadījah, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
He was asked about a mouse falling into a well. He said: If it dies and does not rot and stink, then forty buckets; and if it swells in it and stinks, all of the water is to be drawn out.

So the sound approach regarding what this report contains of the command to draw forty buckets if it has not stunk is that it is to be understood as a form of recommendation, not obligation and requirement, because none of our companions held obligation in this amount.

key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well whose water is subject to purification rulings
key_terms.الْفَأْرَةِ: a mouse, the animal whose fall into the well is being discussed
key_terms.تُنْتِنْ: to emit a foul odor or become putrid
key_terms.فَأَرْبَعِينَ دَلْوًا: the drawing of forty buckets of water
key_terms.نُزِحَ الْمَاءُ كُلُّهُ: all the water is to be drawn out

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a mouse dies in a well according to Shia hadith in al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This report addresses the legal ruling concerning a mouse that falls into a well and distinguishes between cases where it dies without putrefying and where it swells and gives off a foul odor. The accompanying juristic clarification states that drawing forty buckets in the first case is understood as recommended rather than obligatory, reflecting Imami legal interpretation.
